mode.label: Giant
mode.note: 200.0 kg; a tall, lanky giant with long thin legs and arms, a long neck and a narrow frame. Its stride is held to a hunched, lumbering walk: the upper back rounded 18–22°, knees bent, the pelvis rolling and turning, and the arms swinging 32–42° each way, trailing the legs; the search finds the cheapest walk in that style. Simulated with a simpler pipeline than the other bodies (a searched stride, inverse dynamics and static optimization; see How it works). Bipedal walk; the best bipedal run found costs +14% and the best two-footed hop found costs +35%, though this model is less faithful for gaits with a flight phase.

lede: A muscle-driven 3D animal walks on the gait that minimizes its metabolic cost, with its bones kept apart and its head held steady and level. Switch between fourteen bodies: the quadruped, the same body with long forelimbs and broad shoulders, that body with ten legs, a three-legged walker, a six-legged one, four humanoids (a test biped, a thin kid, a lumbering ogre and a lanky giant) and five comic bipeds (a bobblehead, a hooded hunchback, a beanpole, a pear-shaped waddler and a top-heavy brute); everything below follows the selected body. All walk at 1 m/s except the ogre at 0.7 m/s, the hood at 0.6 m/s and the pear at 0.8 m/s.
compareSub: The giant (200.0 kg, 2.90 m) is the biped reshaped: long thin legs and arms, a long neck and a narrow frame.
